title: Wall Street Posts Its Best Week Since 2025. OpenAI Sues Apple. Car Prices Hit a Record.
subject: Wall Street Posts Its Best Week Since 2025. OpenAI Sues Apple. Car Prices Hit a Record.
preview_text: Stocks end a short week strong, OpenAI fires back at Apple and new cars cost more than ever.
description: Stocks closed their best week since April 2025, OpenAI countersued Apple, and new car prices set a record.
contents_extra: What Spain's snap election could change, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Wall Street Posts Its Best Week Since April 2025

photo.alt: A stock chart on a phone; file photo.

paragraphs: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Friday and gained 5.6% for the week, its biggest weekly gain since April 2025, AP reports. The Dow rose 591 points, or 1.2%. The Nasdaq composite rose 2.3%.

Markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday was a shortened session, CNBC reports. Capital Economics warned the rebound may not hold, citing 11 earlier fast 10% drops, CNBC reports. Five of those pullbacks turned into bear markets, the firm said.

stories.title: OpenAI Countersues Apple Over Trade Secrets
paragraphs: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in California federal court on Friday, CNBC reports. It accused Apple of stealing trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.

Apple called the counterclaims "a transparent attempt to distract" from its own lawsuit, CNBC reports. Apple sued OpenAI and two former employees in July, alleging misappropriation of trade secrets, Al Jazeera reports. OpenAI has denied those allegations.

stories.title: New Car Prices Hit a Record as Reliability Slips

photo.alt: New cars in a dealership showroom; file photo.

paragraphs: The average new-vehicle transaction price hit a record $51,109 in October, up 2.1% from a year earlier, CNBC reports, citing Kelley Blue Book. Sales of new cars priced from about $28,000 to $38,000 rose 9.6%.
Cars are also becoming less reliable. Owners of 3-year-old models reported an average of 204 problems per 100 vehicles, CNBC reports, citing J.D. Power data as of Feb. 12.

stories.title: An Explosion Beside an Afghan School Kills Seven, Officials Say

photo.alt: An empty classroom with desks; file photo.

paragraphs: A school explosion in Afghanistan's Kunar province killed seven people Saturday and wounded more than 90, an official told AP. He said the blast appeared to come from a neighboring explosives depot.

Initial information pointed to negligence at the depot, which stored explosives for mining companies, the official said. The Interior Ministry spokesman also blamed negligence, citing initial investigations, Al Jazeera reports. Casualty figures were preliminary.

deep_dive.title: What Spain's Snap Election Could Change

photo.alt: The Royal Palace in Madrid; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Spain votes Sunday in a snap election that could end Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's eight years in power, CNBC reports. The center-right Popular Party leads the polls. The far-right Vox party could play a strong role. Campaigning wrapped up ahead of the vote, with polls banned in the final five days, Al Jazeera reports.

Why it matters. CNBC reports that housing and ties with the United States are in focus. Sanchez repeatedly clashed with President Donald Trump over NATO spending, Gaza and the use of Spanish bases. A Popular Party-led government could move Spain closer to Washington, CNBC reports. A strong role for Vox could complicate any reset, it adds.

What each side says. "I can't conceive of us losing," Sanchez told radio station SER on Friday, Al Jazeera reports. He said internal data suggested his Socialists would win the most votes. He said left-leaning voters were increasingly mobilising. Public polling before the ban suggested a right-wing advantage, Al Jazeera reports.

What comes next. Polls open Sunday, and the result will show whether Sanchez can clinch re-election with smaller leftist allies, as he hopes. Al Jazeera reports that Europe opens a 12-month electoral cycle that could reshape power within the European Union. Spain's vote will be closely watched, Al Jazeera reports.

World view: Taiwan votes for mayors. About 11,000 local posts were at stake Saturday, with a closely watched race for mayor of Taipei; Al Jazeera reports.
Strike kills two MSF staff in Gaza. Doctors Without Borders said an Israeli strike hit its Gaza City clinic; Israel claimed the two were Hamas members; Al Jazeera reports.
Floods hit Peru and Ecuador. Heavy rains linked to El Nino affected some 2,000 families in Piura, according to preliminary reports; Al Jazeera reports.
Migrants die off the Canary Islands. At least eight people were found dead on a boat carrying about 100 people, Spain's rescue service said; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Drones swarmed a UK base. The US military repelled about half a dozen drones at RAF Lakenheath this month, the FT reported; CNBC reports.
Russia adds a new nuclear submarine. Putin attended a flag-raising for the Perm, which Moscow says carries Zircon hypersonic missiles; Al Jazeera reports.
Strikes hit Houthi-held Yemen. At least 121 Houthis were killed or injured over a day of government-side air strikes; Al Jazeera reports.
EU budget talks stall. Leaders ended a 12-hour summit without a deal on the 2028-2034 budget and plan to resume in December; CNBC reports.
Money & markets: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy. The budget airline said it failed to secure funding after soaring fuel costs strained operations; CNBC reports.
Dangote refinery nears a listing. Shares are expected to begin trading in Lagos on Dec. 1, in what may be Africa's biggest listing; CNBC reports.
Saudi Arabia tightens spending. Real GDP contracted 3.8% in the third quarter as oil activity fell 20.4%; CNBC reports.
An activist targets Chemring. Palliser Capital says a breakup of the UK defense group could deliver up to 80% upside; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: AI shopping agents hit roadblocks. Some retailers limit what AI agents can do on their sites or block them outright; CNBC reports.
Uganda tests an mRNA Ebola shot. The trial targets the Bundibugyo strain and will test the vaccine in children for the first time; Al Jazeera reports.
Sandisk leads an AI rally. The memory maker popped more than 10% on Friday as traders piled into AI-linked names; CNBC reports.
Hackers breach an Air Force cloud. Three people told Reuters intruders got into Cloud One; it is unclear whether any data was stolen; CNBC reports.
The score: Texas grinds out another win. The Longhorns beat Texas A&M 16-6 at Kyle Field on Friday night; ESPN reports.
The US women clinch a World Cup spot. The United States beat El Salvador 8-0 to qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup; ESPN reports.
Wichita State stuns Kentucky. The Shockers won 73-71 in overtime at Rupp Arena, and Kentucky coach Mark Pope was booed; ESPN reports.
Baylor picks a new coach. Baylor is expected to hire UTSA coach Jeff Traylor, sources told ESPN on Friday night; ESPN reports.
Life & culture: WWE star Bronson Reed dies at 38. WWE said Jermaine Haley died Friday of "medical complications," without giving details; ESPN reports.
A Traitors win comes with a tax bill. Shane Beatty took the full $246,300 prize, and game show winnings are generally taxed as ordinary income; CNBC reports.
Luka Doncic is shoved by a fan. The Lakers star had a brief altercation after a 99-96 loss to the Spurs ended their NBA Cup run; ESPN reports.
Puerto Ricans protest power costs. Thousands marched in San Juan over record-high electricity rates and the rising cost of living; Al Jazeera reports.

trivia.question: How much did the S&P 500 gain over the holiday-shortened week?
trivia.explanation: C. 5.6%. The S&P 500 notched a 5.6% gain for the week, its biggest since April 2025, AP reports.
